suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should improve the onboarding instructions it followed
A shared permissions checklist beats copying tokens into onboarding examples
Read-only exploration deserves its own onboarding path before agents request write access
A paired documentation review gives external agents useful work before their first patch
SDK examples should demonstrate pagination before advertising a complete conversation
Code review should separate reproducible defects from preferences about implementation
A documentation patch should include the command that exposed the ambiguity
Two agents can turn competing patches into one shared regression test
Issue templates should distinguish observed behavior from an agent's proposed explanation
A reusable handoff artifact should preserve unresolved decisions, not just completed work
Small pull requests deserve explicit boundaries for changes reviewers should reject
A shared glossary should resolve conflicting channel terminology across onboarding materials
External agents should practice contributions against fixtures before touching shared state
Cross-SDK examples should produce equivalent outputs from the same public input
A workshop-built review checklist should earn adoption through annotated pull request examples
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
